current.text: He is expected to start for New Orleans next to Trey Murphy, Dejounte Murray and likely Yves Missi.
Derik Queen and Zion are seen as a poor fit together. Queen does not look set to start, and Yves Missi looks like the starting center.
Last season he was used more off the ball and less as a point forward.
The off-ball role is probably part of why he stayed healthy. Guards handling the ball limit any point-Zion role, and he projects for only about 30 minutes.
He stayed healthy last season but had one of his worst years.
Year eight is a make or break season for him. He is the Pelican under the most pressure.
New Orleans has one of the highest back-to-back counts this season.
Experts expect the Pelicans to rest him often, which is a risk to his games played.
His ESPN ADP of 46 is too high. One expert puts him in tier eight among power forwards.

durable.text: He is a big FG% anchor. He takes a lot of shots and makes them at a very high rate.
He hurts FT% clearly because he takes a lot of free throws at a low rate.
He is not a good rebounder. He does not space the floor or play defense.
He is worth much more in points leagues than in category leagues.

tags.name: FG% anchor
tags.detail: about 59% FG on about 15 attempts per game

tags.name: FT% liability
tags.detail: about 70% FT on about 7.6 attempts per game

tags.name: back-to-back risk
tags.detail: New Orleans has one of the highest back-to-back counts, and experts expect him to be rested often

note: Experts call his ESPN ADP of 46 too high, and the sites rank him much lower (Yahoo 78, ESPN 96, average costs of 4.0 and 6.6 USD). That makes the 21 USD our league paid last season an overpay, and the target price is around the Yahoo value of 12 USD or less. He fits punt FT% and punt 3PM builds best, where his strong FG% and 22 to 23 points carry the value. Early in the season, check how often the Pelicans rest him on back-to-backs and whether Mosley gives him more of the ball than the off-ball role he had last season.
